source1: Shyam Manohar Mishra, Yasovarman of Kanauj: A Study of Political History, Abhinav Publications 1977 (description calls the successors of the Kanauj king 'a most tantalizing problem') - https://books.google.com/books?id=kZWgj-YMdVEC
source2: Rama Shankar Tripathi, History of Kanauj: To the Moslem Conquest, Motilal Banarsidass 1989 (contents treat Cakrayudha as later Kanauj ruler) - https://books.google.com/books?id=2Tnh2QjGhMQC
notes: Lalitaditya of Kashmir defeated Yashovarman c.740 (annexation vs nominal submission disputed); Jain texts give son Ama 749-753; how the line gave way to the Ayudhas (Indrayudha ruling by 783) is undocumented. DB end 780 approximate.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'history of Central Asia' (Uighur empire section) - https://www.britannica.com/topic/history-of-Central-Asia
source2: Michael R. Drompp, 'The Yenisei Kyrgyz from Early Times to the Mongol Conquest', in The Turks vol. 1, Yeni Turkiye 2002 - https://www.academia.edu/10197431
notes: Britannica: Kyrgyz 'put an abrupt end to Uighur rule in Mongolia' in 840; Drompp: renegade Uighur general aided Kyrgyz, kagan killed, capital plundered. Preceded by 839 coup, famine, epidemic, livestock losses. Kyrgyz did not long hold Orkhon.

source1: A. D. H. Bivar, 'Kushan Dynasty i. Dynastic History', Encyclopaedia Iranica 2009 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kushan-dynasty-i-history
source2: Etienne de la Vaissiere, 'Kushanshahs i. History', Encyclopaedia Iranica 2016 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kushanshahs-01
notes: Sasanians (Ardashir I/Shapur I) conquered Kushan lands up to Indus; Shapur I's 262 inscription claims Kushanshahr to Peshawar; Kushanshahs overstruck Kanishka III coins in Gandhara. Rump Kushans east to c.320. DB end 319 too late; conquest dates disputed.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'China: Changes under Kublai Khan and his successors' - https://www.britannica.com/place/China/Changes-under-Kublai-Khan-and-his-successors
notes: Kublai's regime, victorious in 1260-64 civil war with Ariq Boke, moved capital to Dadu and adopted dynastic name Da Yuan in 1271; same court continued. Empire-wide, four khanates became independent c.1261-62 (fragmentation outside core).

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Spain: The caliphate of Cordoba' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Spain/The-caliphate-of-Cordoba
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Abd al-Rahman III' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Abd-al-Rahman-III ; also 'Umar ibn Hafsun' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Umar-ibn-Hafsun
notes: Same Umayyad state: Abd al-Rahman III, emir from 912, proclaimed himself caliph in 929; DB split is relabelling. Prior crisis: Ibn Hafsun's revolt from 879 and widespread rebellions, last resistance ending by 933.

Kassa (Tewodros II), non-noble warlord from within the realm, defeated regional lords (Ras Ali 1853) and was crowned 1855, ending Gonder-based Era of Princes; replaced feudal provincial order with appointed governors. T0 arguable (imperial office continued).

source2: Osman G. Ozgudenli, 'Ottoman-Persian Relations i. Under Sultan Selim I and Shah Esma'il I', Encyclopaedia Iranica 2006 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ottoman-persian-relations-i
notes: Dataset split at 1517 Mamluk conquest; same Ottoman dynasty and state continued under Selim I. Prior crisis: Sahkulu revolt 1511, Selim's 1512 accession through civil strife with brothers and father.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Byzantine Empire: From 867 to the Ottoman conquest' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Byzantine-Empire/From-867-to-the-Ottoman-conquest
source2: Anthony Kaldellis, 'The Byzantine conquest of Crete (961 AD), Prokopios' Vandal War, and the Continuator of the Chronicle of Symeon', Byzantine and Modern Greek Studies 39.2 (2015) - https://doi.org/10.1017/S0307013100015408
notes: Nikephoros Phokas' expedition (960) besieged and stormed Chandax March 961; Byzantines reconquered Crete, emir taken to Constantinople, island made a theme. Emirate's internal history poorly documented. DB start 824 (conquest c.824-827).

Hulegu's Mongol army took Baghdad 13 Feb 1258; caliph al-Musta'sim executed; Iraq became Ilkhanid. Factional and Sunni-Shi'i tension at court but no civil war or large revolt identified in preceding 50 years.

Chandragupta Maurya overthrew Dhanananda's Nanda Magadha c.321 BCE after taking Punjab post-323; whether his army was external or an internal usurpation is debated (T1c possible). Nanda usurpation of Shaishunagas c.345 BCE counted for Q4.
